script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Family
Theme: forgiveness

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. KITCHEN - DAY

JANE (mid 30s, warm, motherly) and her two children, EMMA (12, curious) and SAM (10, mischievous), sit around the kitchen table, drinking milk and eating cereal. Jane looks at the clock on the wall.

JANE
(smiling)
Alright, you two. Time to get ready for school.

EMMA
(excited)
Mom! I finished my science project last night. I can't wait to show Mrs. Thompson!

SAM
(grinning)
I made a funny in math yesterday. Mrs. Davis laughed so hard.

JANE
(proudly)
I'm so proud of both of you.

INT. SCHOOL - DAY

Emma and Sam walk into the school building, arm in arm. They part ways at the hallway, heading to different classrooms. Jane watches from the front entrance, waving as the doors close behind them.

INT. LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

Jane sits on the couch, surrounded by her laptop, papers, and a pile of unread books. Her phone rings. She answers.

JANE
Hello?

A pause. Jane's eyes widen in shock.

JANE
Sam? Is everything okay?

SAM
(shaking)
Mom... I didn't mean to. I'm so sorry.

INT. SCHOOL - DAY

A flashback to earlier in the day. Sam is in the cafeteria, playing a prank on another student. The student retaliates, spilling a tray of food on Sam. Sam becomes enraged and a food fight breaks out.

INT. LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

Jane listens, concerned.

JANE
Sam, tell me what happened at school today.

SAM
(tearfully)
I was just trying to be funny, mom. But then... I don't know, I lost control.

INT. SCHOOL - DAY

Another flashback. Sam is suspended from school, sitting in a quiet corner of the hallway, looking remorseful.

INT. LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

Jane listens, feeling a mix of emotions.

JANE
Sam, I know you didn't mean to hurt anyone. But we need to talk about consequences and forgiveness.

INT. COUNSELOR'S OFFICE - DAY

Jane sits in the counselor's office, holding a box of tissues. She listens intently as the counselor explains the school's restorative justice program.

INT. CLASSROOM - DAY

Emma sits at her desk, frowning. A knock at the door interrupts her thoughts. Sam enters, looking embarrassed.

SAM
Emma, I'm so sorry for what I did. Can you forgive me?

Emma looks up at her brother, unsure.

EMMA
I don't know. You really messed things up.

INT. KITCHEN - DAY

Jane sits at the table, surrounded by her family. They eat breakfast together, discussing Sam's apology to Emma and the consequences of his actions. They share stories of forgiveness and the importance of making amends.

INT. SCHOOL - DAY

The last scene shows Emma extending her hand to Sam in the hallway, a smile on her face. Sam takes her hand, and they walk to their next class, arm in arm.

FADE OUT.

THE END
